key_insight: Dynamic transformation of 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) couples crystallization control with interface passivation in lead-free tin perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: A single additive offers a route to more uniform absorber films and lower interfacial recombination, improving photovoltaic efficiency and operational stability.
method: PX carbonyl groups coordinate with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and moderate crystal growth.
Annealing transforms PX in situ into species suggested to carry amidinium functionality.
Transformed species preferentially passivate surface A-site vacancies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
watch_item: The transformed species are not definitively identified in the abstract, and performance at manufacturing scale remains unestablished.
paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
